stories.title: Fifty creators bring GeoGuessr charity cup to its final day
paragraphs: A three-day online GeoGuessr cup brought 50 Hungarian creators together to raise money for five-year-old Alíz Pencz's treatment. Its final, featuring 18 qualifying pairs, is scheduled for October 25.

The organizer says the duos compete by guessing locations, with teams advancing through rounds rather than being eliminated by one poor guess. The format lets less experienced streamers reach the final too.

The event site reports HUF 6.88 million raised through its donation page. The organizer says Alíz's family is seeking treatment abroad after a brainstem tumor diagnosis; GeoCup is a voluntary community fundraiser, not an official GeoGuessr event.

scoreNotes.general: A coordinated creator event tied to a substantial, concrete medical fundraiser, with activity continuing today.
scoreNotes.heat: The 50-streamer roster and multi-day finale make this more than a routine individual broadcast, though the audience is regionally focused.
scoreNotes.time: The online cup runs October 23–25, with its final on October 25 inside the current window.
scoreNotes.ethos: The organizers document the schedule, format, beneficiary, and donation total. The event is community-run and is not an official GeoGuessr competition.

stories.title: Ninja-led Gaming for Cause raises $240,850 for cancer support
paragraphs: Ninja led the second annual Gaming for Cause, a 24-hour creator livestream on October 22 for skin-cancer prevention, early detection, and supportive care. The relay included streamers in several countries and live segments with medical experts.
The campaign site reports that the event raised $240,850 for the Union for International Cancer Control and partner organizations, including Melanoma Institute Australia.

Ninja has spoken publicly about surviving melanoma twice. The event uses gaming communities to combine entertainment, fundraising, and health information; the reported total is the organizer's figure.

scoreNotes.general: A prominent international creator event combined large-scale livestreaming with health education and a reported six-figure donation result.
scoreNotes.heat: The campaign's stated 67-million-follower host and international creator relay signal broad reach; the total raised is a point-in-time organizer figure.
scoreNotes.time: The 24-hour broadcast took place October 22, within the preceding seven days but before the current 24-hour window.
scoreNotes.ethos: The organizer and a contemporaneous release describe the event and its beneficiaries. The fundraising amount comes from the campaign site, not an independent audit.

stories.title: Arkane Lyon faces a November buyer deadline as Microsoft weighs options
paragraphs: Arkane Lyon, the French studio behind Dishonored and Deathloop, is seeking a buyer as Microsoft explores options for the team. PC Gamer reports that the consultation period has been extended by a month, with November 13 identified as a key deadline.

Microsoft told PC Gamer it is looking for a partner to support the remaining development of Marvel's Blade. The company said the consultation documents describing a possible closure are required process documents, not a final shutdown decision.

The studio employs 217 people, according to the reporting. A sampled r/gaming discussion showed strong concern about the studio and Blade, while comments also debated whether a buyer would preserve the team or only acquire its intellectual property.

scoreNotes.general: The potential loss of a veteran studio and uncertainty around a major Marvel game place this among the week's most consequential industry developments.
scoreNotes.heat: Arkane Lyon employs 217 people and made Dishonored and Deathloop; the reported process also puts Marvel's Blade at risk.
scoreNotes.time: The reporting surfaced October 23. The buyer-search deadline has been extended, so the process remains active rather than resolved.
scoreNotes.ethos: PC Gamer reports Microsoft's statement and cites Le Monde's reporting and documents. Microsoft says the consultation documents do not represent a final decision to close the studio.

stories.title: GameMaker will let developers sell GMRT games without a Professional license
paragraphs: GameMaker says its next-generation runtime, GMRT, will be free for commercial use starting January 1, 2027. Developers will be able to make and distribute GMRT games on desktop, mobile, web, and GX Games without buying a Professional license.
The change also gives source-code access to every tier. Console exports still require an Enterprise license and approved-developer status, and GameMaker says existing tier prices will not change.

GMRT remains in beta. The move could reduce the entry cost for indie projects while giving developers more ability to inspect and adapt the runtime; it does not make every GameMaker service or console export free.

scoreNotes.general: A meaningful change to the cost and source-access model of a widely used indie development tool, with clear limits for console exports.
scoreNotes.heat: It could lower an up-front barrier for smaller developers, but it affects one engine and the new runtime is still in beta.
scoreNotes.time: Announced October 23 and due to take effect January 1, 2027; this is a seven-day fallback development, not a fresh 24-hour change.
scoreNotes.ethos: GameMaker's own announcement gives the effective date and licensing terms; Creative Bloq independently explains the change.

nearMisses.title: GothamChess questions a viral smart-glasses chess stunt
nearMisses.reason: A topical creator reaction, but the evidence is concentrated in one report about an unverified social-media stunt, with no ruling or confirmation that a sanctioned chess match was involved.

scoreNotes.general: The story connects a high-profile chess creator to debate about smart glasses and AI-assisted play, but remains a narrow online episode.
scoreNotes.heat: Dexerto described the video as widely shared and reported reactions across platforms, without a representative audience measure.
scoreNotes.time: The report appeared October 23, within the preceding seven-day fallback period.
scoreNotes.ethos: GothamChess questioned the presentation; the apparent cheating claim and the full technical setup are not independently verified.

paragraphs: Chess YouTuber Levy 'GothamChess' Rozman criticized a TikTok video that claimed to show its creator using Ray-Ban Meta glasses, AI, and a chess engine to win a park game.

Rozman questioned the demonstration, pointing to an inactive-looking chess clock and a known opening trap that could beat a novice quickly. The reporting does not establish that the game was a rated match or a confirmed cheating case.
The episode raises questions about wearable cameras and discreet computer assistance, but the video is not independent proof of the process it depicts.

citations.title: GothamChess blasts TikToker's viral Meta glasses chess cheating stunt
